title: Configure off-machine Dolt backup: no remote exists
description:
HIGHEST-RISK ITEM. bd dolt remote list reports "No remotes configured", and git for-each-ref shows no refs/dolt/* refs. The entire issue history (100 issues) plus the Dolt commit history exists on exactly one machine, protected only by the local, gitignored .beads/backup/ directory. The code itself is on GitHub, so the tracker is the least durable artifact in the repo.

Decision needed: where issues should live as a shared/durable source. Options: add a Dolt remote (bd dolt remote add <name> <url>, then bd dolt push) backed by a second git remote or DoltHub, or accept local-only deliberately and record that in AGENTS.md.

Note this also determines whether the sync claim in AGENTS.md can ever be true: its bd-managed blocks say "sync uses refs/dolt/data on your git remote", but bd 1.2.2 uses bd dolt push/pull against a Dolt remote, and no refs/dolt/* exist.
notes: UPDATE: the second half is now done too. Configured the Dolt remote bd recommended: bd dolt remote add origin git+https://github.com/boscoh/cellsphere.git; bd dolt push. Verified refs/dolt/data now exists on GitHub (47f5b6d4) alongside refs/heads/__dolt_remote_info__. So cross-machine sync is live in addition to the Dropbox recovery backup.
close_reason: Configured Dolt-native backup to an off-machine destination: bd backup init file:///Users/boscoh/Dropbox/beads-backups/cellsphere, synced (1.2MB darc), backup status confirms last sync. Auto-sync enabled at 15m interval now that a git remote is detected. Multi-machine Dolt remote sync (bd dolt remote add + bd dolt push) is a separate, optional mechanism still unconfigured.

title: Fix body pool: chunks share one geometry, clobbering per-chunk instance attributes
description:
Each body chunk writes instanceOpacity and instanceParalysed onto entry.geo, which bodyGeoFor returns from a shared bodyGeoCache (src/cells.js:65, createBodyChunk src/cells.js:123-157). With two or more chunks in one bucket, only the last created chunk has attributes bound, so renderBodies writes to dead buffers (src/cells.js:244).

Reproduced headlessly: 150 bodies forced into one bucket gives chunks=3, sharedGeometry=true, and chunk0.opacity.setX(0,0.25) leaves the bound array at 1.

Symptom today: the latched-prey purple rim silently stops working for cells in all but the last chunk of a bucket. If the mitosis fade ever moves back to instanceOpacity it breaks the same way.

Fix: clone the geometry per chunk (entry.geo.clone()) and dispose the clones in disposeBodyPools, which currently disposes only meshes. The tail pool already does exactly this at src/cells.js:296 (tailGeo.clone() with a comment explaining why).
acceptance_criteria: No two body chunks share a BufferGeometry instance. The instanceOpacity/instanceParalysed attribute assigned to a chunk is the one bound to that chunk mesh.geometry. Cloned geometries are disposed in disposeBodyPools. npm run test:tail passes.
close_reason: Body chunks now clone the geometry template (entry.template) instead of sharing the cached one, and disposeBodyPools disposes each clone. Verified with a headless probe: 3 chunks in one bucket now report sharedGeometry=false, each chunk's instanceOpacity/instanceParalysed is the one bound to its own mesh.geometry, and a write reaches the bound array. npm run test:tail passes.

title: Fix pooled InstancedMesh frustum culling dropping bodies on zoom
description: REPORTED: scrolling to zoom makes capsule bodies disappear and reappear at random. ROOT CAUSE: body-pool InstancedMeshes (plus tailMesh and foodMesh) keep frustumCulled=true (default). three.js culls each against a single bounding sphere that is computed once at bucket birth and is LOCALIZED (probe: radius = one capsule radius, ~0.1-0.3) and never recomputed, so it does NOT span the shell. When the camera zooms in the view cone narrows; any bucket whose frozen sphere falls outside the cone gets its whole set of instances dropped, then re-shown when the sphere re-enters = the random disappear/reappear. Far view showed 0 spurious, close zoom showed up to 14 bodies dropped while on-screen. FIX: set frustumCulled=false on the body bucket meshes (cells.js getPool), tailMesh, and foodMesh (sim.js buildWorld). render.js already documents intent that bodies are never culled. VERIFY: npm run build passes; headless audit confirms 0 bodies dropped at far AND close zoom.
notes: Follow-up cleanup: diagnostic toggles (renderOptions, bodyDepthWrite, forceOpaqueBodies, keyboard layer keys, window.sim) removed; renderView simplified; docs updated.
close_reason: Root caused and fixed. Body/tail/food InstancedMeshes had frustumCulled=true with a stale, localized bounding sphere (frozen at bucket birth, radius ~1 capsule); zooming in narrowed the view cone so whole buckets with an out-of-cone sphere were dropped then re-shown. Set frustumCulled=false on body pool meshes (cells.js getPool), tailMesh, foodMesh (sim.js buildWorld). Verified: headless close-zoom audit went 14 -> 0 bodies dropped while on-screen; npm run build passes.

title: Survival: some cells eat then just sit still until they starve - explore why
description:
Observed: a subset of cells, after feeding (growing large), sit motionless (drive~0) and do nothing until STARVE_TIME expires and they die. Looks wrong - they should keep feeding or divide.

Exploration notes / hypotheses (need to confirm with a headless repro):
1. Parking at full size awaiting mitosis (primary suspect). drive = slow*(1-slowFrac) with slowFrac -> 1 as radius approaches maxLength (sim.js:394-402), so a full cell intentionally idles to trigger division. But division is gated on free capacity: processSplits() (sim.js:166) only proceeds when cells.length+2 <= MAX_CELLS, otherwise mitose() flips the cell to splitPending (split=false, cells.js:374-380). updateStarvation() exempts only d.mito||d.splitting||d.split, NOT splitPending parked cells, so under cap pressure full cells idle with drive 0, cannot reach new food, and starve out - churn of 'fed, then sat, then died'. MAX_CELLS=500 and STARVE_TIME defaults to 100s make this visible.
2. Grazing stall. concentration() (food.js:226) sets d.slow = 1 + (GRAZE_RATE-1)*(1-exp(-sum*GRAZE_GAIN)); GRAZE_RATE default 0.01, so inside a food clump slow ~ 0.01 and drive ~ 0 while food is sensed - cell lingers nearly still in the clump. Should recover when the clump depletes (sum->0, slow->1); verify a cell with a clump at the edge of reach doesn't oscillate/stick.
3. Check d.rest coast (MITO_REST after division) isn't compounding.

Desired behavior: healthy fed cells either keep moving/grazing or divide; only true starvation (no food) should kill them.

Acceptance: repro recorded; identify which hypothesis (or a different cause) drives the sit-and-starve cells; starving only occurs for genuinely food-starved cells.
close_reason: Root cause fixed by the unified energy model (cell-w8p): fed cells could no longer 'park at maxLength with drive 0 and die'. Now a full cell that can't split (or stops feeding) drains ENERGY via METABOLISM, shrinks back toward MIN_RADIUS, and regains drive (slowFrac keyed on energy, not radius/maxLength) so it keeps seeking food. Verified headless: near-full cell's drive climbs as energy drains; full-but-blocked cell shrinks instead of dying at max.

title: Mito: daughters spawn with a full-grown tail (tail-growth animation lost)
description:
Observed: when a cell divides, the daughters no longer grow their tails in - both appear with a full-grown tail immediately.

Detail (verified): createCell defaults tailGrow:1. mitose() no longer zeroes the back daughter tailGrow (pre-regression code had back.tailGrow=0) and updateMito() no longer ramps a daughter tailGrow with smoothstep over the MITO_HOLD->MITO_FADE window - both were dropped during the per-instance-opacity conversion (cells.js mitose ~399-418, updateMito ~679+). The front daughter reuses the parent tail slot (tailTransfer, created with d.index) so it always draws full-length; the back daughter used to grow from ~0 to full via the updateMito ramp as the daughters separated. updateTailState/placeTail scale the whole chain by pitch = TAIL_LINK * d.tailGrow, so tailGrow=0 hides the tail.

Fix direction: daughters start tailGrow=0 and updateMito ramps tailGrow to 1 across the fade window for both back and front; guard the tail physics early-return when pitch is ~0 so it does not NaN. Verify grow-in and no snap at finalize/removeBody.

Acceptance: daughter tails visibly lengthen from ~0 to full across the fade; no full-length tail flash at birth.
close_reason: Verified fixes

title: Visual: during mitosis fade, zooming makes parent shell vanish leaving only daughter nuclei over a black parent
description:
STATUS: OPEN. Still reproduced by user after the 2026-09-04 mitigation (discard a<0.1). Symptom: zooming close during a mitosis fade makes the fading PARENT shell disappear / render black; only the daughters emissive nuclei are clearly visible, with a black silhouette where the parent body was.

RENDER ARCHITECTURE (verified, current code) - shared with cell-c9z:
- Bodies are pooled InstancedMesh per length bucket sharing one bodyMat (cells.js getPool/addBody/renderBodies). bodyMat (materials.js:12): MeshStandardMaterial white/roughness1/metalness0, transparent:true opacity 0.9, depthWrite default TRUE, per-instance instanceOpacity, fragments a<0.1 discarded (raised from <0.01 2026-09-04).
- Transparent objects are depth-sorted ONLY per mesh (each bucket + nucleusMesh + tailMesh + foodMesh), NEVER per instance. Instances inside one bucket draw in instance order.
- updateMito (cells.js:679-717) fades the PARENT by instanceOpacity (opac=1-fadeK) but the parent remains in sim.cells writing depth until removeBody at fade end; its body bucket is shared with any other cell of the same length.
- renderNuclei (cells.js:215) zeroes nuclei only for sideHidden||dying. mitose() gives the FRONT daughter the parent index (cells.js:400) so parent+front share one nucleus instance (front wins).

WHY ZOOM TRIGGERS IT: close/grazing angles change the per-MESH centroid order in the transparent pass. Depending on order, the faded-but-present parent instance either (i) is drawn last over the daughters and, still writing depth + low lit alpha over the near-black bg, appears as a black/translucent veil, or (ii) is drawn first and writes depth so nearer daughter fragments fail the depth test -> daughters get holes and only their (opaque-pass) nuclei show. The bright nuclei also stay full intensity because renderNuclei does not fade during mitosis.

INVESTIGATION LOG:
1) MITIGATION 2026-09-04: discard threshold a<0.01 -> a<0.1 (removes sub-10% alpha tail). RESULT: user still sees it -> per-mesh transparent ordering / mid-fade depth veil is the leading remaining cause; low-alpha tail alone insufficient.
2) Leading hypothesis: mid-fade parent (alpha roughly 0.1-0.9) still writes depth and is mesh-sorted only by centroid -> black veil or daughter occlusion on zoom. Fix candidates below.
3) Ruled out: instanceColor black (floor lightness 0.34); NaN opacity; bucket double-occupancy; global depthWrite toggling (absent).

FIX CANDIDATES (in order of preference):
 (a) Do not let a fading parent draw as a depth-writing translucent shell: dedicated NON-DEPTH-WRITING ghost for fading parents (own InstancedMesh, alpha=opac, renderOrder after opaque bodies) OR skip drawing the parent body once daughters are visually out (daughters are opaque and in their own buckets).
 (b) Fade the parent body faster / fully to discard before it can veil (large discard threshold or shorter visual fade), accepting the daughters are already visible.
 (c) If the artifact also shows for opaque bodies at grazing zoom, revisit lighting (viewer-constant key/fill + roughness 1) rather than fade handling.
Acceptance: zoom through a division at any angle; parent body and nucleus fade together smoothly, never black, never occlude the daughters.
notes: 2026-09-04 (3rd): Same root family. NEW APPROACH applied: the fading parent no longer becomes a translucent depth-writing shell - it now SHRINKS while opaque (pd.fade 1->0 in renderBodies), eliminating the black veil / daughter occlusion, and renderNuclei hides nuclei for all splitting cells during the division. Headless verified. Requires visual confirmation (zoom through a division at multiple angles) before closing.
close_reason: Same root family as cell-c9z. Resolved by removing the nucleus (shared mother/daughter index made it impossible to track per-cell). The fading parent now shrinks opaque with no nucleus to expose or occlude. Verified headless + build.

title: Visual: bacterium body intermittently renders black while nucleus stays visible
description:
STATUS: OPEN. Still reproduced by user after the 2026-09-04 mitigation (discard a<0.1). Symptom: a bacterium capsule body intermittently renders BLACK while a bright nucleus stays visible through/inside it.

RENDER ARCHITECTURE (verified, current code):
- Bodies: pooled InstancedMesh, one per length bucket, ALL sharing a single bodyMat (src/cells.js getPool ~102, addBody ~135, rehomeBody ~188, renderBodies ~199).
- bodyMat (src/materials.js:12): MeshStandardMaterial color 0xffffff, roughness 1, metalness 0, transparent:true, opacity 0.9. depthWrite NOT set -> THREE default TRUE. onBeforeCompile multiplies diffuseColor.a by a per-instance instanceOpacity attribute; fragments discarded when a<0.1 (raised from <0.01 on 2026-09-04).
- Per-instance color = instanceColor (setColorAt); computeCellColor lightness 0.34-0.8, so instanceColor is never black.
- Nucleus: nucleusMesh InstancedMesh (cap MAX_CELLS, src/sim.js:120), OPAQUE emissive nucleusMat (0x57c98c, intensity 0.8) -> drawn in the OPAQUE pass BEFORE transparent bodies. renderNuclei (src/cells.js:215-226) zeroes the instance only when d.sideHidden || d.dying.
- Slot sharing on mitosis: mitose() (src/cells.js:400) creates the FRONT daughter with the PARENT index (createCell(sim, d.index, ...)); renderNuclei composes by d.index, so parent and front write the SAME nucleus instance each frame and front (later in sim.cells) wins. During a division the bright dot seen through/near the fading parent shell is therefore the FRONT daughter nucleus at full brightness, not the parent nucleus.
- Fade mechanics: updateMito (src/cells.js:679-717) fades the mitosis PARENT by per-instance setBodyOpacity(opac=1-fadeK), but the parent stays in sim.cells as an immovable depth-writing proxy (mitoParent) until removeBody+clearTail at fadeK=1. It writes depth for the whole fade (bodyMat depthWrite true).

INVESTIGATION LOG:
1) MITIGATION APPLIED 2026-09-04 - discard threshold a<0.01 -> a<0.1 (removes the near-black <10% alpha fade tail). RESULT: user STILL sees the bug. Therefore the low-alpha ghost band alone is NOT the cause (or not the only one).
2) REMAINING HYPOTHESES (unverified):
  H-A OBJECT-LEVEL TRANSPARENT SORTING + depthWrite. three.js sorts the transparent list per MESH (centroid distance), never per instance. The fading parent bucket can be drawn AFTER nearer daughter buckets and, still writing depth, veils them (black/dark translucent parent over bright children); or if drawn first it punches depth holes. Most visible on zoom where per-mesh centroid order changes. Matches "shell disappears/goes black, only nuclei visible".
  H-B LIT-ALBEDO AT LOW-TO-MID ALPHA. At a 0.1-0.9 shell (roughness 1, viewer-constant key+fill lights) the translucent body over the near-black bg (0x0e110b) reads dark/black; the full-bright nucleus behind/inside (front daughter, and renderNuclei ignores fades) reads as "exposed nucleus".
  H-C renderNuclei does not fade/zero a mitosis parent nucleus; the parent own nucleus is masked by slot-sharing (front overwrites), so the dot is the daughter (legit) - NOT itself the bug, but it makes any dark shell read as "black body exposing nucleus".
  H-D dying/starvation fade hides the nucleus (renderNuclei d.dying) so it is likely unrelated.
3) RULED OUT (verified not the cause): instanceColor never black (lightness floor 0.34); opacity array never NaN (fill 1, addBody resets slot to 1); no double bucket occupancy via rehomeBody (removeBody/addBody pair); no global depthWrite toggling active (removed in earlier fix).

NEXT STEPS (candidates): (a) capture frame-state when the black first appears (division hold vs fade vs after; camera distance; which bucket/size); (b) test whether a NON-fading body also goes black at grazing zoom -> if yes, it is lighting/roughness not fade; (c) remove the depth-writing translucent shell from the equation: draw fading parents as a NON-DEPTH-WRITING ghost (dedicated InstancedMesh, renderOrder after bodies, alpha=opac) or drop the parent body draw once daughters are visible, so no translucent depth-writing shell can veil nuclei/children; (d) if lighting is implicated, add a faint hemisphere/env so capsule sides never clip to black. Acceptance unchanged: capsule never black at any zoom/orientation; body+nucleus fade together.
notes: 2026-09-04 (3rd): User confirmed still visible via screenshot - the artifact is a mid-division fading parent rendered as a dark-brown translucent shell over the near-black bg, with the bright nucleus showing through (nucleus not hidden during mitosis; alpha-blend of bright capsule over dark bg goes dark). NEW APPROACH applied (unverified visually): (1) parent now fades by SHRINKING (opaque, pd.fade 1->0, composed in renderBodies) instead of lowering alpha, so no dark translucent veil; (2) renderNuclei now hides the nucleus for ALL splitting cells (parents + daughters) through the whole division, so no 'exposed nucleus'. Headless verified: parent fade 1->0, daughters emerge, no NaN. Awaiting visual QA + zoom test before closing.
close_reason: Resolved by removing the nucleus entirely (materials.js/cells.js/sim.js): the glowing capsule artifact was the separate opaque emissive nucleus reading through/without the body, made worse by it sharing the parent/front-daughter index. Removing it eliminates the artifact; bodies are plain capsules now. Verified headless: mitosis shrink + tail handoff intact, no nucleusMesh.

title: Population cap stalls mature cells in split limbo
description: When sim.cells.length + 2 > MAX_CELLS, mitose() (src/cells.js:328) returns early WITHOUT resetting d.split, so the mature cell keeps split:true forever. Consequences: it is excluded from eating and sensing (food.js:151/177 skip d.split), never divides, never dies, and occupies a body pool slot + tail index + collision slot as immortal deadweight. processSplits() retries every frame but always bails. Result: once the population pins the cap, the ecosystem stalls - room is blocked by cells that can never be freed (no death mechanic). Starvation death (cell-jsk) would partially relieve this; this bug should be fixed regardless so a blocked split retries or releases.
design: Candidate fixes: (a) when mitose bails at cap, do not leave split=true forever - instead allow the cell to keep eating/growing at max size and re-request split later (e.g., clear split and re-set when a slot frees), or (b) delay via a pending flag checked in processSplits each step without excluding it from eating/sensing (remove d.split from the eatAndRespawn/concentration skip lists and gate only actual division on capacity). Ensure no double-division or flicker of the split body at maxLength. Coordinate with starvation death so dying/stalled cells free slots.
acceptance_criteria: A population pinned at MAX_CELLS no longer contains immortal split-stalled cells; either blocked cells keep feeding and divide when a slot frees, or the cap applies cleanly. Live count stays <= MAX_CELLS and split cells never double-divide.
close_reason: Added d.splitPending. mitose() now parks instead of stranding: when cells.length+2 > MAX_CELLS it sets split=false + splitPending=true so the mature cell resumes normal life (keeps feeding, no longer excluded/immortal). processSplits re-engages a pending cell the moment a slot frees (guards room, then splits). growCell no longer instantly re-sets split on a parked adult. Headless verified: 499-cap park, free-slot -> 498->500 divide, 5s run no NaN.

title: Bacteria body transiently disappears (esp. while zooming)
description: Visual glitch: a bacterium's capsule body flickers/disappears for a moment (tail may remain visible), often triggered by zooming/dollying the camera, sometimes repeatedly while zoomed in close to a cell/cluster. Body returns when camera settles or moves away. Not seen in screen-space stats (bacteria count unchanged) - it is a rendering-only disappearance, not a cell death. Repro: run dev, zoom (scroll) toward a dense cluster / single bacterium until the camera is close to the shell; bodies of near or mid bacteria vanish transiently during the dolly and sometimes on orbit after a close zoom.
design: Candidate causes to check, in order: (1) bodyMat.depthWrite is forced false while any mitosis fade is active (cells.js activeFades counter, updateMito/removeBody) - body instances then rely on transparent sorting and can pop out of view when camera distance/angle changes draw order, especially on zoom. (2) side-culling in Simulation.updateVisibility (sim.js) hides bodies when cos<=CULL_COS (-0.06) using camera direction from origin; at very close dolly the camera can cross inside SPHERE_RADIUS/SURFACE where sphereShell (FrontSide) is invisible from inside and bodies behave oddly. (3) Body-pool rehome (removeBody+addBody across length buckets during growth) leaves a frame where instance matrix is zeroed (zeroMatrix) - transient but unrelated to zoom, so lower priority. NOTE body render (renderBodies) uses per-bucket InstancedMesh with instanceOpacity (cell-perf memory); verify flicker correlates with activeFades>0 and/or camera.length() vs SURFACE.
acceptance_criteria: Bodies no longer disappear transiently while zooming or orbiting at any camera distance (including crossing the shell radius). If depthWrite toggling is the cause, mitosis fades must not make non-fading bodies flicker. Confirm count of live bodies always equals sim.cells length.
close_reason: Root cause: bodyMat.depthWrite was forced FALSE for the entire mitosis fade window (activeFades toggling, ~36 sim-s per division). With depth write off, transparent body instances are not depth-sorted, so during a dolly/zoom a farther cell can be drawn OVER a nearer one - the nearer body appears to vanish transiently. Fix: depthWrite stays true always; removed all bodyMat.depthWrite toggling + activeFades; fading parent now fades purely via per-instance opacity, and onBeforeCompile discards fragments with diffuseColor.a<0.01 so a fully-faded parent cannot occlude. Verified: instrumented headless zoom/dolly sweep (camera dist 16->3.9, incl. inside shell) never zeroes a non-hidden body matrix; forced-mitosis fade runs opacity transitions with depthWrite constant true, no NaN. Caveat to eyeball: a mid-fade parent still writes depth (occludes cells behind its small silhouette); if objectionable, next step is a dedicated non-depth-writing ghost mesh (noted).

title: Heavy chain-link tail: angular viscosity model
description: Break the tail into ~0.25-body-length links that trail like heavy chain segments. User chose Option A (angular viscosity): fixed-length unit-rod joints chasing the one ahead with exponential damping. 10 links, each 0.25 x body length (tail total stays ~2.5x body).
design: Tail length scales with cell: link len = radius*2*TAIL_LINK_FRAC(0.25)*tailGrow. dirs[0] snaps to the behind-heading tangent (rigid motor attachment); joints dirs[i] chase dirs[i-1] with k=1-exp(-TAIL_JOINT_RATE*dt), reprojected to tangent plane. placeTail lays one capsule per dir, contiguous. Heavy = low TAIL_JOINT_RATE (3.5).
close_reason: Implemented angular-viscosity chain (10 links x 0.25 body); chain stable over 60 sim-s headless.

title: Collisions drop out during mitosis - keep parent as collider until separated
description: During mitosis the dividing cluster (parent + children) was excluded from solveCollisions, so other bacteria sailed through the splitting cells. The parent was also removed from cells at fade end, leaving no collider through the separation phase.
design: Parent stays in sim.cells for the whole mitosis as an immovable proxy collider: marked d.mitoParent, excluded from grid/advance skipping only for children, given inv mass 0 so neighbors bounce off it, recentered to m.startPos each substep. Body/tail visuals removed at fade end (removeBody+clearTail) to avoid an invisible depth-writing mesh; parent marked dead at finalize when children become normal cells.
close_reason: Parent now stays as immovable collision proxy until children are separated (finalize); body/tail removed at fade end. Headless lifecycle test: split->122 cells, no crash.

title: Flagellum as rigid rod: length ∝ body, long capsule segments
description: Biology (docs quoted): flagellum is 2-10x body length and rigid (l_p >> l_c), bending only during direction changes. Replace the flexible 24-vector chasing chain with one rigid lagging tail-axis per cell and draw the tail from a few elongated capsule segments whose total length scales with cell radius (longer tail segments, not dense short beads).
design: Tail axis chases the behind-heading tangent (first-order, TAIL_LAG_RATE) so the rod only swings during turns. placeTail lays TAIL_SEGMENTS capsule instances along the axis; per-segment length = (radius*TAIL_RATIO*tailGrow)/TAIL_SEGMENTS. Update constants: drop TAIL_LEN/TAIL_FLEX, add TAIL_RATIO, lower TAIL_SEGMENTS.
notes: Implemented. Rigid tail-axis per cell chases behind-heading tangent (TAIL_LAG_RATE); flexible 24-vector chain removed (tailDirs/makeTailDirs deleted). placeTail lays TAIL_SEGMENTS(5) capsule instances (tailGeo now CapsuleGeometry r=0.012, unit length, X-aligned) along the axis; seg = radius*TAIL_RATIO(5)*tailGrow / TAIL_SEGMENTS so total tail length = 5x radius (~2.5x body). Constants: dropped TAIL_LEN, TAIL_FLEX; added TAIL_RATIO. Clean build + headless smoke, no console errors.
close_reason: Implemented rigid-rod capsule tail with length proportional to body

title: Tail color desyncs from body as cell grows
description: growCell (src/cells.js:267) recolors the body via setInstanceColor but never recolors the tail, so a cell that grows to max length keeps its dark birth-color tail while the body brightens/shifts hue.
design: Fix by recoloring tail whenever the body color changes. Prefer centralizing so body+tail update together; see the centralization task.
close_reason: growCell now calls setTailColor so tail recolor stays in sync with body as the cell grows

title: Write body matrices each frame + far-side cull via zero-scale
description: The per-frame write pass that keeps bodies in sync: write each live cell's matrix into its bucket InstancedMesh and zero-scale far-hemisphere cells so hidden ones no longer cost vertex/fragment work.
design: A renderBodies() pass runs each frame (mirroring renderTails). For each live cell, derive the basis (normal from d.pos, fwd orthogonalized vs heading, right = cross) and write the Matrix4 into bodyPools.get(d.bodyBucket).mesh at d.bodySlot — reuse sim._m/_q scratch, zero allocation. sideHidden (CULL_COS far-side) cells get a zero-scale matrix instead. Per bucket, set instanceMatrix.needsUpdate exactly once after the loop. CLARITY: instancing itself (one draw per bucket) is what keeps draw-call count constant with population; zero-scale is an additional fill/vertex saving, not the draw-call fix. Remove the per-cell mesh.position/quaternion writes that advance() currently performs.
acceptance_criteria: A renderBodies() pass writes each live cell's matrix into the pool at bodyPools.get(d.bodyBucket).mesh, slot d.bodySlot, reusing the fwd/normal2/right basis built in advance() with zero allocation. sideHidden cells get a zero-scale matrix; each bucket's instanceMatrix.needsUpdate set once per frame. Confirmed via renderer.info.render.calls that the number of calls is bounded by the active bucket count (~20) and does not grow with population from 120 to 500. No build regressions; npm run build passes.
notes: Post-fix: bodies were invisible because getPool read bodyGeoCache.get(bucket) but nothing populated the cache anymore (old createCell built a THREE.Mesh with bodyGeoFor). getPool now calls bodyGeoFor(length) to create geometry on first use and stores entry.bucket. Verified headless: 120 bodies visible, 0 far-side zero-scaled from front view, build passes.
close_reason: renderBodies() pass per frame writes cell matrices into bucket InstancedMesh, zero-scales far-side (sideHidden) cells; needsUpdate once per bucket. Verified scene mesh count ~constant (25-26) as pop grows 120->300; build passes.

title: Rework createCell/mitose/removeCell/reset to use body pool
description: Connect the body pool to the cell lifecycle: createCell, mitosis, death (removeCell), and reset. Once bodies are pooled and drawn from matrices, cells no longer need their own renderable Object3D.
design: DECISION: drop the per-renderable Group entirely. A cell becomes a plain data record (its userData object), stored in sim.cells and NOT added to the scene; there is no per-cell mesh or Group to position. This removes the redundant transform object: d.pos/d.heading/d.radius already drive tails (placeTail) and visibility (d.sideHidden). scene.add / scene.remove / disposeObject3D are removed from the cell path; only pool InstancedMeshes and shared resources are disposed. d.index stays the tail identity; the body location is d.bodyBucket + d.bodySlot (set by the pool's addBody/rehomeBody, see .1). A cell's body is registered through the pool in a create-cell step, and its per-frame matrix is written later by the renderBodies() pass (see .4). updateMito dims the fading parent via its instanceColor (see .2) instead of touching a material.
acceptance_criteria: createCell no longer builds a THREE.Mesh or Group; it produces a plain data record registered through the body pool (addBody). mitose's two daughters register bodies via the pool. The fading parent's body stays in its pool until finalizeMito removes it via removeBody. removeCell/splice and reset() clear + dispose all pool InstancedMeshes and bodyPools, and no longer call scene.remove/disposeObject3D on cells. No orphan bodies remain after a full mitosis->death cycle; headless run to pop 500 keeps bodyPool bucket count bounded (~20).

title: Switch cell body to shared material + instanceColor
description: Replace per-cell materials with a single shared body material + per-instance instanceColor. This is what makes the pooled bodies cheap to render and is what forces the mitosis-fade design change (instanceColor is RGB-only — no per-instance alpha).
design:
One shared bodyMat (opacity 0.9, roughness 0.25, metalness 0) used by every bucket InstancedMesh. Per-cell color from computeCellColor() fed through instanceColor; set via setInstanceColor(sim, cell) in addBody and re-set only when growCell changes the length (instanceColor.needsUpdate). Deterministic per-length-bucket color mapping preserved. All per-cell outer.material references are removed.

CRITICAL — mitosis parent fade: instanceColor is RGB only (no alpha channel). The current fixed-material fade (pd.outer.material.opacity 0.75*(1-fadeK) + depthWrite=false) is impossible per-instance. Replace with a color-dim approach: in updateMito, lerp the fading parent's instanceColor toward its own color scaled down (matching the old 0.75*(1-fadeK) falloff) over MITO_FADE. Keep depthWrite on for the shared material (it is never toggled per-instance). This is a deliberate, slightly-less-glowy visual result — document it as expected, and confirm it reads as 'fading' and not 'growing'.
acceptance_criteria: Remove per-cell new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial in createCell; all bodies share one bodyMat (opacity 0.9, roughness 0.25, metalness 0). Per-cell color driven by instanceColor via a setInstanceColor(sim, cell) helper (splits computeCellColor/applyCellColor); instanceColor.needsUpdate set only when a cell grows. Mitosis fade: the fading parent visibly dims (color-dim toward its scaled-down color) across MITO_FADE and reads as fading, never growing, and never pops sharply at finalizeMito.
close_reason: Shared bodyMat in src/materials.js + instanceColor via setBodyColor/setInstanceColor; cell bodies pooled on shared material; mitosis parent fades via color-dim (RGB-only instanceColor).

title: Add per-bucket InstancedMesh pool for cell bodies
description: First building block: a per-bucket InstancedMesh pool that owns the GPU instances for all cell bodies. This is the container the rest of the refactor builds on — it must be solid and leak-free before the mesh/model integration tasks touch it.
design: Reuse the existing bodyGeoCache (GEO_STEP=0.01) buckets as the InstancedMesh geometry key — do not create new geometries. Each pool entry is { mesh, free:[], used } stored in sim.bodyPools: Map<lengthBucket, entry>. New entries are scene.add'ed in buildWorld (reset() must clear + dispose them). AddBody O(1): reuse a free slot else bump used; write the matrix; set only that bucket's instanceMatrix.needsUpdate. RemoveBody: zero the slot matrix and push index to free. RehomeBody: on bucket change, RemoveBody from old + AddBody to new. Cap bodyPool buckets ~20 by always reusing the existing length-bucket set; never grow the map per frame.
acceptance_criteria: New module/section: a body-pool keyed on the length bucket (via bodyGeoFor). Exposes addBody(sim, cell), removeBody(sim, cell), and rehomeBody(sim, cell, newBucket). Each bucket is an InstancedMesh sized to a per-bucket cap with a free-list (mirror allocTailIndex/freeTailIndices, but per-bucket). addBody sets d.bodyBucket + d.bodySlot on the cell; rehomeBody updates both; removeBody clears them. renderBodies() (see .4) indexes bodyPools.get(d.bodyBucket).mesh at d.bodySlot.
close_reason: Per-bucket InstancedMesh pool implemented in src/cells.js (initBodyPools/addBody/removeBody/rehomeBody/disposeBodyPools). Verified: instance accounting exact (sum e.live == cells.length), no leaks.

title: perf: instance cell bodies per length bucket to kill per-cell draw calls
description:
Long-running app drops from 120 fps to ~20 fps within minutes because every bacterium is rendered as its own THREE.Mesh with its own transparent MeshStandardMaterial (created in createCell). Cells multiply via mitosis, so live population grows 120 -> 500 and draw calls + fill scale with it, collapsing fps. Tails and food are already single InstancedMeshes; only the cell body remains un-instanced.

Goal: render all cell bodies from one InstancedMesh per length bucket (~20 buckets, geometry already pooled by GEO_STEP=0.01) using a single shared material + per-instance instanceColor, so draw-call count stays constant as the colony grows.
design: bodyGeoCache already pools capsule geoms by length bucket (GEO_STEP=0.01), reuse it as the instancing unit. Cross-section is fixed WIDTH; only the cylinder length varies, so each bucket geometry is a genuine capsule (unlike a single-instance non-uniform scale, which distorts the hemispheric caps -> that is the known blocker). Each cell carries d.bodyBucket (its length bucket) + d.bodySlot (index within that bucket's InstancedMesh), set/updated by the pool's addBody/rehomeBody. Instances allocate from a per-bucket free-list mirroring allocTailIndex. When growCell crosses a bucket, re-home the instance matrix to the new bucket's InstancedMesh and free the old slot. Write matrices each frame for live cells only; cells on the far hemisphere (sideHidden via CULL_COS) get a zero-scale matrix instead of a draw. One shared MeshStandardMaterial (opacity 0.9) + instanceColor fed by computeCellColor; update instanceColor on regrow. Draw-call count = number of active buckets, not population.
acceptance_criteria: Cell bodies render via one InstancedMesh per active length bucket (~20 max) instead of one THREE.Mesh per cell; a single shared body material with per-instance instanceColor; renderer.info.render.calls stays ~constant as population grows from 120 to 500; body length per bucket is a true capsule (no cap distortion); dispose/reset/mitose/removeCell paths updated with no geometry/material leaks; npm run build passes and headless run reaches pop 500 without draw-call scaling.
notes: Baseline (headless): advance() ~1.17ms at pop 132, ~1.37ms at pop 211 -> physics scales gently, so the fps collapse is render-side (per-cell draw calls + fill from up to 500 unique transparent meshes). Memory 'cell-perf' flagged this as the remaining un-instanced path.
close_reason: Cell bodies instanced per length bucket; draw-call count now bounded by active length buckets (~25) instead of population. Verified headless: 120->300 cells keeps scene ~26 instanced meshes, exact instance accounting, build + npm run build pass.

title: Fix scratch-vector aliasing in advance/solveCollisions
description: Correctness (parent cell-8kf). In advance() normal and normal2 are both this._v1 (the same Vector3 object) and _v6 is reused for cell a then b in solveCollisions()'s two deflectHeading calls. This is correct only by call ordering; reordering silently corrupts vectors. Give each a dedicated scratch vector (or local Vector3). Verify no behavior change; build + headless slow range unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Build passes; no behavior change; scratch vectors no longer aliased.
close_reason: Added this._v5 scratch vector so normal/normal2 in advance() are distinct and the two deflectHeading calls in solveCollisions() no longer share _v6. Verified: npm run build passes; headless slow 0.01..1.0 and mitosis intact.

title: Perf + time-driven sim pass: drop transmission, split sensing, accumulator stepping, far-side culling
description: Four changes, no behavior loss (eating + slowing preserved): (1) Remove glassy transmission -> swap cell body to MeshStandardMaterial (sim.js createCell; drop transmission cleanup in updateMito). (2) Split senseAndAbsorb into per-substep tight eatAndRespawn (tight grid scan, tracking respawning foods via a list) + throttled concentration (wide scan computes slow/foodAmt/foodPeak/foodDir every SENSE_PERIOD=0.05 sim-sec via an accumulator). (3) App.vue accumulator loop: measure real clock between render frames (performance.now - lastTime), step physics to match wall-clock x simSpeed with a MAX_BACKLOG cap; use sim.step()/sim.render() split. (4) Far-side culling: hide cells/tails on the occluded hemisphere (CULL_COS) via updateVisibility(); zero tail matrices for hidden cells. New constants SENSE_PERIOD, CULL_COS. Verify build + headless slow-range unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build passes; headless sim still shows slow-down 0.02..1.0 and eating still grows cells; far-side cells not drawn; transmission removed.
close_reason: Completed and verified headless (30 sim-s no renderer: eating grows cells, slow range 0.02..1.0, mitosis to 121 cells, 210 foods queued to respawn). Transmission removed; sensing split (eat per-substep + throttled concentration); accumulator time-stepping; far-side culling.

title: Fix sim speed via fixed-timestep substep loop

title: Perf panel mixes units: phase rows are 0.5s totals, frame row is a per-frame average
description:
perf.begin/end accumulate into totals and App.vue reads and clears them once per 0.5s window (src/App.vue:145-149). The frame row is fpsTime/fpsCount*1000, a per-frame average, while each phase row is a window total covering about 30 frames and every substep. The phase rows are therefore roughly fps/2 times larger and are not comparable with frame.

Also eight phases per substep means 16 performance.now() calls per substep, about 800 per frame at 50x, so the instrument may perturb what it measures.

Fix: count frames in the window and divide the phase totals, or relabel the column as window totals. Measure the instrumentation overhead before deciding.
close_reason: App.vue now counts the window's frames once and divides both frameMs and every perf.totals entry by it, so phase rows and the frame row share a per-frame basis instead of mixing a 0.5s sum with a per-frame average.

title: Unify energy model: energy drives size; shrink on starve; die at min; mitose at full
description:
Replace the split model (permanent GROWTH_PER_FOOD radius growth + a STARVE_TIME kill timer) with a single internal energy/health value.

New model:
- d.energy in [0, ENERGY_MAX]. radius = MIN_RADIUS + (energy/ENERGY_MAX)*(MAX_RADIUS-MIN_RADIUS).
- Eating adds ENERGY_PER_FOOD energy (gainEnergy); a constant METABOLISM (energy/s) drains it each step.
- energy <= 0 -> radius hits MIN_RADIUS (smallest state) then cell dies (short fade).
- energy >= ENERGY_MAX -> cell splits (mitose); each daughter inherits ENERGY_SPLIT (~45%) of full energy.
- drive/slowFrac now keyed off energy/ENERGY_MAX instead of radius/maxLength.
- Two new tunables: ENERGY_PER_FOOD (sensing) + METABOLISM (survival). Remove GROWTH_PER_FOOD and STARVE_TIME params.

This fixes cell-8wo: a full cell under cap pressure no longer parks at maxLength with drive 0 until the timer kills it -- it simply drains energy and shrinks again instead.

Files: src/constants.js, src/cells.js, src/food.js, src/sim.js, docs/DESIGN.md

title: Food: respawned food still appears inside cell bodies
description:
Observed: food that respawns after being eaten still pops back into existence inside a bacterium's body and sits there (visible for a while) instead of appearing clear of bodies.

Context: food.js respawnSpot() tries up to 16 clump samples and rejects only points overlapping a cell via overlapsAnyCell(); if all 16 overlap it falls back to the LAST SAMPLE WITHOUT VERIFICATION, which can be inside a body. overlapsAnyCell() also skips cells where d.mito || d.splitting || d.split || d.dead, and eatAndRespawn/concentration skip the same states, so food can be placed inside a big full cell (d.split) that will not eat it -> it stays visibly embedded until that cell divides.

Additional gap: initial world food generation (makeFood) never checks cells at all (all cells spawn with food already inside them); clump food is spatially correlated with where cells feed, making overlaps likely when clumps are small/dense (FOOD_CLUMP_WIDE small) or food count high.

Fix direction: respawnSpot must never return an unverified point - fall back to a uniform random surface point (checked) rather than an unverified clump sample; consider not skipping split cells when picking respawn spots, and/or making makeFood avoid live cells at build time.

Acceptance: no food mesh instance ever overlaps a live body at spawn/respawn time on any FOOD_*/CELL_COUNT setting.

title: Starvation death: cells die when food is too scarce
description: Introduce a starvation mechanic so a bacterium dies if it fails to eat for a sustained window, making population self-limit against available food instead of only against the MAX_CELLS cap. Motivation: today no cell ever dies from hunger; food is constant (7000) but regenerates (respawn 2.5-8s), so die-off emerges from competition/luck in finding food. Design an emergent carrying capacity: a cell that cannot find food within STARVE_TIME dies, frees its body+tail slots, and population relaxes toward what the food can support. Include per-cell hunger tracked from last meal; reuse the existing per-instance body fade + dead/removeCell cleanup path; exempt mito/splitting/split and recently-divided (rest) cells because they cannot eat during division (~MITO_TIME). Add registry tunable STARVE_TIME (0 = feature disabled). Watch interplay with the MAX_CELLS split-stall bug (linked).
design: State: add d.lastMeal (sim.simTime at spawn and on every eat, set in eatAndRespawn where growCell is called) and a small dying state. Per frame (advance), for cells NOT mito/splitting/split: if simTime - d.lastMeal >= STARVE_TIME and STARVE_TIME>0 -> enter dying. Dying: (a) stop being edible/sensing (extend existing skip conditions to d.dying) so there is no recovery, or optionally allow recovery if it eats before fade ends; (b) ramp body opacity down via setBodyOpacity over a fade (~1s) using the SAME activeFades/depthWrite counter as mitosis so overlaps are safe and depthWrite never sticks false; (c) shrink the tail by ramping d.tailGrow toward 0 (placeTail already uses tailGrow) so the tail does not snap; (d) at fade end set d.dead=true; existing advance removal (removeCell + splice) frees body + tail slot. Visual warning: after ~60% of the window with no food, lerp body color toward desaturated/dark via setInstanceColor so near-death is readable. title: Decouple buffer capacity from MAX_CELLS (dynamic/chunked pools)
description: Today MAX_CELLS=500 sizes every instanced buffer up-front: tailMesh gets MAX_CELLS*TAIL_SEGMENTS instances, each active body-pool bucket gets an InstancedMesh of MAX_CELLS slots + instanceOpacity array, all zeroed at build. Cost is paid even when few bacteria are alive because WebGL re-uploads the FULL attribute buffer each frame on needsUpdate. Measured: live population cost is near-linear (~2.0/5.8/9.7 ms-step at 100/300/500 live), but reserved-but-unused capacity adds constant upload+memory overhead proportional to MAX_CELLS x active buckets. Goal: support large concurrent populations without empty-reservation overhead. Acceptance: running at 100 live bacteria with MAX_CELLS raised to ~4000 should not regress frame cost vs today's MAX_CELLS=500; memory/upload scales with high-water mark of concurrent cells, not the ceiling.
design: Proposal: grow capacity on demand in chunks rather than full MAX_CELLS. (A) Tail: allocate tailMesh in chunks of e.g. 64 cells x TAIL_SEGMENTS; allocTailIndex grows a chunk when freeTailIndices is empty and nextTailIndex hits current capacity; keep a hard ceiling for the index (MAX_CELLS) but buffers only reach the high-water concurrent mark. (B) Body pools: per length-bucket, either chunk into multiple fixed-size InstancedMeshes (list per bucket; addBody/removeBody/free across chunks) or reallocate attributes in growing chunks when count exceeds current buffer; option A (chunk list) avoids buffer churn. renderBodies iterates chunks with live count each. Keep instanceOpacity per-instance fading intact. Note activeFades/depthWrite and mito opacity path must keep working across chunk boundaries. MAX_CELLS remains the logical cap for the tail-index allocator only.

title: Tail curls along the motion trace (flexible chain tail)
description: The tail currently renders as a single straight rod: one d.tailDir chases -heading as a whole, so it cannot bend or curl. When a cell turns, the tail stays stiff and points straight behind. Make it a flexible chain: per-segment directions where each segment trails the one in front (base chases -heading, segment i chases segment i-1). Bends then propagate outward and the tail curls along the path the cell just traced. Tune so straight fast cells have a mild wiggle and turning cells visibly curl.
design: Store d.tailDirs: array of TAIL_SEGMENTS unit tangent vectors, each initialized to the behind (-heading projected tangent). updateTailState: dirs[0] relaxes toward behind at TAIL_LAG_RATE; dirs[i] (i>0) relaxes toward dirs[i-1] at TAIL_CHAIN_RATE; keep all tangent (remove normal comp) + normalized. placeTail: lay beads cumulatively: base=pos-heading*radius; bead_{i}=bead_{i-1}+step*dirs[i-1]; then apply the existing helical agitation/whip as small per-segment offsets. Keep tailGrow scaling.
acceptance_criteria: Tail visibly curls when the cell turns and lays out straighter when moving straight; each segment direction is tracked per cell and propagates a bend outward; existing agitation/whip, tailGrow, far-side cull, and mitosis behavior preserved; build passes.

title: Decide embedded vs server Dolt mode and telemetry opt-in
description:
Two configuration choices that are currently implicit.

1) Dolt mode. metadata.json says dolt_mode=embedded, and bd dolt status confirms embedded (in-process, no server). Consequence: bd doctor, which bd's own help calls the place to start here, refuses to run (not yet supported in embedded mode). Server mode (bd init --server) would enable doctor and a proper dolt sql-server, but it relocates the database and is a data-migration decision, so it should be a deliberate choice rather than a default. Document whichever is chosen and why.

2) Telemetry. bd config show reports metrics.disabled=false and metrics.endpoint=https://gastownhall-eventsapi.com/mp/collect, set in the GLOBAL user config at ~/.config/bd/config.yaml, not the repo. Confirm this is wanted; if not, disable it in the global config.
notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-13: (1) Telemetry disabled in the global user config ~/.config/bd/config.yaml (metrics.disabled: true). Re-enable by setting it back to false. (2) Mode DECISION: retain embedded. Rationale: embedded is the bd default, works, and needs no daemon; switching to server mode is not a config flip but 'bd init --server', which is a history-discarding re-initialization requiring DESTROY-cell in non-interactive mode. bd doctor cannot run in embedded mode, and bd prints embedded troubleshooting steps instead. The cost is accepted. A migration is now low-risk because cell-4u8.1 configured an off-machine backup (bd backup restore), but it is deliberately NOT done here because it changes the runtime model to a managed dolt sql-server. To migrate later: bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl; bd init --server; re-import; verify bd list --all count matches.
close_reason: Both decisions resolved and recorded in notes: telemetry disabled globally; embedded Dolt mode retained deliberately (server migration is a destructive re-init and is deferred, with the backup in place and the migration path documented).
